items.passage: Because a dollar of tax saved is equally valuable whether it reduces a payment or increases a refund, standard economic models predict that taxpayers minimizing their liability should be ______ which outcome they anticipate. Economist Alex Rees-Jones, however, found that filers expecting to owe money reduced their liability more than comparable filers expecting refunds.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To be indifferent to something is to have no reason to prefer one outcome over the other. The text explains that a saved dollar is equally valuable whether it reduces a payment or increases a refund, so the standard models expect taxpayers’ efforts not to depend on which outcome they anticipate. The word “however” then introduces Rees-Jones’s finding as a departure from that prediction.

A.recipe: reversal: describes the finding, not the prediction (ANT)
A.why_wrong: Filers did respond to whether they owed money, which is what Rees-Jones found; the blank, though, describes what the standard models predict, and “however” marks the finding as the opposite of that prediction.

B.recipe: near miss: not knowing instead of not caring (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: The models do not assume that taxpayers fail to know whether they owe money or expect a refund; they assume that knowing it should make no difference, since a saved dollar is worth the same either way.

D.why_wrong: Being wary of something means being cautious or suspicious about it. The models’ prediction rests on the equal value of a saved dollar in either case and says nothing about taxpayers’ caution; it implies the outcome should not matter to their decisions at all.

sources.what: Rees-Jones, Quantifying Loss-Averse Tax Manipulation, Review of Economic Studies 85(2), 2018: taxpayers facing a payment on tax day reduce their tax liability by about $34 more than taxpayers owed a refund

items.notes: Subject: social science (behavioral economics). Key letter C. Steps: 2 (the first clause gives the premise that makes owing and a refund equivalent, so effort should not depend on them; “however” confirms that the finding is the opposite). Key in a transferred, technical sense (indifferent to, as economists use it). Two distractors partly right: attentive to is what filers actually were; unaware of sounds like indifference but names not knowing. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): attentive to 7,136; unaware of 8,556; indifferent to 2,479; wary of 10,734; 1 of 4 past 10,000, 0 past 20,000.

band7.why: Raw ranks (freq.txt): attentive to 7,136; unaware of 8,556; indifferent to 2,479; wary of 10,734: 1 of 4 past 10,000, mean log 3.80, no distractor past 50,000. Plain common key with two-step reasoning (premise, then however), the band-6 B6 pattern (an exhaustive, a modest). Fair band 6.

items.passage: The Mundurucu, an Indigenous people of the Brazilian Amazon, have limited access to formal schooling, and their language contains few geometric terms. Nevertheless, in Véronique Izard’s experiments, Mundurucu adults estimated that a triangle’s angles on a perfectly flat surface total roughly 180 degrees, matching mathematically educated adults—evidence that an understanding of Euclidean geometry can be ______.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Intuitive means known without being taught or reasoned out step by step. The Mundurucu have limited schooling and few geometric terms, yet their estimates matched those of mathematically educated adults. Their understanding of the geometry therefore did not come from instruction, which is what an intuitive grasp is.

A.recipe: near miss: right field, wrong degree (CONNOT)
A.why_wrong: Rudimentary means basic or undeveloped. The Mundurucu lack schooling and vocabulary, but their estimates matched those of mathematically educated adults, so the text gives no sign that their grasp is crude.

B.why_wrong: Provisional means temporary or subject to later change. Nothing in the text suggests that the Mundurucu adults’ understanding is held only for the time being.

C.recipe: reversal: contradicted by the match with other adults (ANT)
C.why_wrong: Idiosyncratic means peculiar to an individual or group. The Mundurucu answered just as educated adults elsewhere did, so their grasp is shared, not peculiar to them.

sources.what: Izard, Pica, Spelke, Dehaene, Flexible intuitions of Euclidean geometry in an Amazonian indigene group, PNAS 2011: Mundurucu adults’ estimates of a triangle’s angles on a planar surface summed to about 180 degrees and converged with those of mathematically educated adults, revealing an intuitive understanding without formal education

items.notes: Subject: social science (cognitive science). Key letter D. Steps: 2 (combine the lack of schooling and vocabulary with the match to educated adults; together they rule out crude or peculiar knowledge and leave knowledge without instruction). Clue is a paraphrase in a different register (limited access to formal schooling) a sentence away from the blank. Distractors: one near miss (rudimentary, tempting because of the missing vocabulary), one reversal, one unsupported. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): rudimentary 22,834; provisional 26,070; idiosyncratic unranked; intuitive 20,681; 4 of 4 past 10,000, 4 past 20,000.

fixes: band_target raised from 6 to 7: the option set passes the band-7 rarity checks (see band7)

band7.why: Raw ranks: rudimentary 22,834; provisional 26,070; idiosyncratic unranked; intuitive 20,681: 4 of 4 past 20,000, mean log 4.77, rarest distractor unseen (check 2), key past 20,000 and 3+ options past 10,000 (check 3), key not the rarest (band-5 guard clear). Two steps, clue in another register a sentence away (limited access to formal schooling), one near-synonym distractor failing on degree (rudimentary): the section-5 B1 recipe. Weakest point: intuitive is the most familiar option.

items.passage: Because precise facial mimicry—replicating the subtle details of another individual’s expression—had been documented only in humans and great apes, researchers widely assumed that such sophisticated communication emerges exclusively in ______ species. In 2019, however, Derry Taylor and Marina Davila-Ross reported precise mimicry among playing sun bears, even though adult sun bears spend most of their lives alone.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Gregarious means living in groups or seeking the company of others. The sun bear finding is presented as a challenge (“however”) to the earlier assumption, and what makes it a challenge is that sun bears mostly live alone. So the assumption must have tied complex mimicry to species that live together, that is, gregarious ones.

A.recipe: reversal: trait of the other side of the contrast (ANT)
A.why_wrong: Reclusive describes the sun bears themselves, which spend most of their lives alone. The blank describes the species the old assumption was about, which the sun bears are contrasted with.

C.why_wrong: Sedentary means staying in one place or inactive. The text never links mimicry to how much animals move, and the fact that sun bears live alone would not challenge such a view.

D.why_wrong: Garrulous means excessively talkative, a trait of speakers rather than of how a species lives. The text contrasts the earlier view with bears that live alone, so the assumption concerned social living, not chattiness; facial mimicry is not speech in any case.

band7_moves: blank on the received view being challenged, with the finding’s side described only by a paraphrase (spend most of their lives alone)
direction left implicit: no antonym of the key appears; the reader infers it from the concessive “even though”
described side’s trait offered as a reversal (reclusive)
near-synonym-field distractor that fails on one feature (garrulous: talk, not group living)

sources.what: University of Portsmouth news release on Taylor, Hartmann, Dezecache, Te Wong, Davila-Ross, Scientific Reports 2019: sun bears showed precise facial mimicry in play; only great apes and humans were previously known to show such complexity; it is widely believed that complex communication occurs only in species with complex social systems, yet the sun bear is not a social animal

items.notes: Subject: natural science (animal behavior). Key letter B. Steps: 2 (the received view is stated without its key trait; the concessive clause about bears living alone shows which trait the view assumed). Concessive frame: yes (even though). Band-7 check 1: 4 of 4 options past 10,000. Band-5 guard: clear (key not the rarest; reclusive is unranked). Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): reclusive unranked; gregarious 29,890; sedentary 35,765; garrulous 17,695; 4 of 4 past 10,000, 3 past 20,000.

band7.why: Raw ranks: reclusive unranked; gregarious 29,890; sedentary 35,765; garrulous 17,695: 4 of 4 past 10,000, 3 past 20,000, rarest distractor unseen, key past 20,000; guard clear (reclusive is the rarest). B3 received view with the blank on the challenged view and its trait left implicit, concessive even though, wrong-party reversal (reclusive) and a sound-alike near miss (garrulous), as in e8fb0744 and 22a41819.

items.passage: Biologist Steven Portugal and colleagues determined that a secretary bird’s kick strikes a snake with roughly five times the bird’s body weight, maintaining contact for only about 15 milliseconds. Such a brief strike cannot be ______ once initiated, so the bird must visually establish its target beforehand—an exacting requirement when the prey is venomous.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To redirect something is to change its course or aim. Because the kick is over in about 15 milliseconds, the bird has no time to change its aim during the strike; that is why, as the text says, it “must visually establish its target beforehand.”

B.recipe: near miss: changes force, not aim (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: The text does mention the kick’s force, but the consequence it draws is about aiming in advance. Being unable to add force mid-kick would not explain why the bird must establish its target beforehand.

C.why_wrong: Nothing in the text concerns whether the kick can be noticed by the snake or by observers, and that would not explain why the bird must aim beforehand.

D.why_wrong: To rehearse is to practice beforehand, which cannot happen “once initiated” in any case; the text says nothing about practice.

sources.what: Phys.org report on Portugal, Murn, Sparkes, Daley, Current Biology 2016: secretary bird kicks reach about five times body weight; contact lasts about 15 milliseconds; once a kick has started the bird cannot adapt it; the bird relies on visual targeting and feed-forward control; a missed strike on a venomous snake could be deadly

items.notes: Subject: natural science (biomechanics). Key letter A. Negated frame stated plainly (cannot be), as in bbb77c84 (unlikely to be superseded). Steps: 2 (the brevity of the kick plus the consequence clause, aim fixed beforehand, pin a change of aim during the kick). Near miss strengthened is tempting because force is the first fact given. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): redirected 73,456; strengthened 7,002; detected 5,405; rehearsed 17,273; 2 of 4 past 10,000, 1 past 20,000.

band7.why: Raw ranks: redirected 73,456; strengthened 7,002; detected 5,405; rehearsed 17,273: 2 of 4 past 10,000. The key rank is a corpus artifact (redirect is a modern word the 1850 to 1928 corpus undercounts), and key-rarest with two distractors under 10,000 is the band-5 guard shape, so no band-7 credit for vocabulary. Negation stated plainly (cannot be), as in band-6 bbb77c84; two steps. Band 6 on reasoning.

items.passage:
The following text is from a 1916 translation of Aleksandr Kuprin’s 1905 novel The Duel. Romashov, a young officer, has come to visit Nikoläiev, a fellow officer, and his wife.

Nikoläiev sat with his back to them at the table that was almost hidden by piles of books, drawings, and maps. Before the year was out he had to make another attempt to get admitted to the Staff College, and for many months he had been preparing with unremitting <u>industry</u> for this stiff examination in which he had already twice failed.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “industry” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: As used in the text, “industry” means diligence, or steady hard work. Nikoläiev’s table is buried in books, drawings, and maps, and he has been preparing “for many months” without a break for an examination he has already failed twice; “unremitting industry” describes that persistent effort.

A.why_wrong: Industry can mean the making of goods, as in a nation’s industry, but Nikoläiev is studying for an examination, not producing anything.

B.why_wrong: Erudition means deep learning, which the piles of books might suggest, but the text describes how hard Nikoläiev is working, not how much he knows; having failed the examination twice, he is still trying to master it.

C.recipe: near miss: economic sense of the target, output instead of effort (CONNOT)
C.why_wrong: Productivity is the amount a worker produces, a meaning tied to industry in its economic sense. The text says nothing about what Nikoläiev’s study has yielded; “unremitting” describes the constancy of his effort.

band7_moves: common word in a sense that is not its first one today (industry = diligence)
one distractor is the target’s everyday sense (Manufacturing), one an economic sense close to it (Productivity), one a topic word from the scene (Erudition)
key itself mid-frequency (Diligence), not a plain everyday synonym

sources.what: Text of The Duel by A. I. Kuprin (London: George Allen & Unwin, first published in 1916), Project Gutenberg 44117; excerpt copied exactly from the scene of Romashov’s visit to the Nikoläievs

items.notes: Subject: literature. Key letter D. Two consecutive sentences copied exactly. The original Russian novel (Poedinok) appeared in 1905. Band-7 check 1: 4 of 4 options past 10,000. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): Manufacturing 12,300; Erudition 25,341; Productivity 42,307; Diligence 14,216; 4 of 4 past 10,000, 2 past 20,000.

band7.why: Raw ranks: Manufacturing 12,300 (10,971 by stem); Erudition 25,341; Productivity 42,307; Diligence 14,216: 4 of 4 past 10,000, 2 past 20,000, mean log 4.31; check 2 not met (no distractor past 50,000); guard clear. Common target in a secondary sense, rare clue word (unremitting 24,828), mid-frequency key, distractors a real sense, an economic-sense near miss and a topic word, the M1 shape of 6557f7fc and 7f935017. Borderline: a student who owns industrious solves it at once.

items.passage: In experiments by psychologists Igor Grossmann and Ethan Kross, people reasoned more wisely about a friend’s relationship problems than about their own, more readily admitting what they did not know. But when people viewed their own problems from a distanced, third-person perspective, the researchers found no ______ between the two kinds of reasoning.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: A disparity is a difference or inequality. The text first describes a gap: people reasoned more wisely about a friend’s problems than about their own. “But” signals that taking a distanced perspective changed this, so the researchers no longer saw a difference between the two kinds of reasoning.

A.why_wrong: An affinity is a likeness or natural connection. Saying the researchers saw no affinity would mean the two kinds of reasoning were unlike each other, but distancing is presented as removing the gap, not widening it.

C.why_wrong: A rivalry is a competition. Nothing in the text suggests that the two kinds of reasoning competed with each other; the point is whether one was wiser than the other.

D.why_wrong: Friction is conflict or tension. The text compares how wisely people reasoned in two situations; it never suggests the two kinds of reasoning clashed, so the absence of friction is not what distancing produced.

sources.what: Grossmann and Kross, Exploring Solomon’s paradox, Psychological Science 2014: participants reasoned more wisely (recognizing the limits of their knowledge and the importance of compromise) about another person’s problems than their own; self-distancing eliminated this asymmetry

items.notes: Subject: social science (psychology). Key letter B. Negator in the blank’s sentence (no), the medium pattern. Steps: 2 (identify the gap described in the first sentence, then undo it under “But” and “no”). Clue in the previous sentence. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): affinity 17,131; disparity 28,960; rivalry 15,093; friction 17,693; 4 of 4 past 10,000, 1 past 20,000.

items.passage: Sociologist Lauren Rivera interviewed 120 people who hire for elite US banks, law firms, and consulting firms and found that evaluators were often ______ cultural fit. More than half ranked a candidate’s similarity to existing employees—in leisure pursuits, background, and self-presentation—as the most important interview criterion.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To be swayed by something is to be influenced by it. The text says that more than half of the evaluators ranked a candidate’s similarity to current employees, that is, cultural fit, as the most important criterion in interviews, so their judgments were strongly influenced by it.

B.why_wrong: Being dismissive of cultural fit would mean treating it as unimportant, but most evaluators ranked it as the single most important criterion.

C.why_wrong: Nothing suggests that evaluators did not know what cultural fit was; they used it deliberately when judging candidates.

D.why_wrong: The text reports how evaluators ranked their criteria, not how they felt about them, and gives no sign of embarrassment.

sources.what: ScienceDaily (American Sociological Association release) on Rivera, Hiring as Cultural Matching, American Sociological Review 2012: 120 interviews at elite investment banks, law firms, and consulting firms; cultural fit, defined as similarity to existing employees in leisure pursuits, background, and self-presentation, was ranked by more than half of evaluators as the most important criterion at the interview stage

items.notes: Subject: social science (sociology). Key letter A. Restatement in the next sentence. Steps: 1. Verb + preposition options with academic-register distractors. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): swayed by 5,327; dismissive of unranked; unfamiliar with 8,144; embarrassed by 4,505; 1 of 4 past 10,000, 1 past 20,000.

items.passage: Roughly 36 years after Italian wall lizards were introduced from one Croatian islet to another, biologist Anthony Herrel and colleagues found that the transplanted population had undergone ______ change. Its head shape, bite strength, and digestive anatomy had diverged from those of the source population about as much as such traits typically differ among separate species.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Wholesale means extensive and affecting many things at once. The next sentence lists changes in head shape, bite strength, and digestive anatomy and says they were about as large as differences between species, so the lizards changed broadly and deeply.

A.why_wrong: Cosmetic means affecting only the surface. The changes reached bite strength and digestive anatomy and were as large as differences between species, so they were far from superficial.

B.why_wrong: Seasonal means tied to the time of year. The text compares the population with its source after 36 years and says nothing about changes that come and go with the seasons.

D.why_wrong: Fleeting means brief. The differences built up over 36 years and are compared to those between separate species, so they are lasting, not passing.

sources.what: Herrel et al., Rapid large-scale evolutionary divergence in morphology and performance associated with exploitation of a different dietary resource, PNAS 2008: about 36 years after experimental introduction, lizards differed in head morphology, bite strength, and digestive tract structure, changes that parallel those documented among species and even families of lizards

items.notes: Subject: natural science (evolutionary biology). Key letter C. Restatement in the next sentence. Steps: 1 (three traits and a species-level scale restate breadth and depth). Key in a less common sense (wholesale = sweeping, not the trade sense). Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): cosmetic 46,826; seasonal 45,224; wholesale 12,092; fleeting 9,174; 3 of 4 past 10,000, 2 past 20,000.

items.subtype: Blank completion: cause or consequence clue
items.passage: Martu hunters in Australia’s Western Desert set small fires while pursuing sand monitor lizards, and the resulting patchwork of burned and unburned ground benefits the lizards, which are densest where the two meet. Because this benefit outweighs the toll of the hunting itself, Rebecca Bliege Bird and colleagues found, intense Martu hunting actually ______ local lizard populations.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To bolster is to strengthen or increase. The text says the patchwork created by hunting fires benefits the lizards and that this benefit outweighs the toll of the hunting, so on balance intense hunting leaves more lizards, not fewer; “actually” marks this as the surprising result.

A.why_wrong: Depleting the population would mean the toll of hunting wins out, but the text says the benefit of the burning outweighs that toll.

B.recipe: near miss: wrong kind of effect (CONNOT)
B.why_wrong: Stabilizing means keeping a population steady. The text describes a benefit that outweighs losses, which implies an increase, and says nothing about steadiness over time.

C.why_wrong: Nothing in the text concerns hiding the lizards; the burned patches affect how many lizards there are, not how visible they are.

sources.what: Bliege Bird, Tayor, Codding, Bird, Niche construction and Dreaming logic: aboriginal patch mosaic burning and varanid lizards (Varanus gouldii) in Australia, Proceedings of the Royal Society B 2013 (full text): Martu hunters in the Western Desert burn while hunting sand monitors; sand monitor populations are higher where Aboriginal hunting is most intense, driven by higher densities near successional edges created by burning; the positive effects of burning while hunting overwhelm the negative effects of predation

items.notes: Subject: social science (anthropology and ecology). Key letter D. Cause and consequence: a because clause sets the balance of benefit against toll, and the blank names the result. Steps: 2 (weigh benefit against toll; “actually” confirms the counterintuitive direction). Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): depletes unranked; stabilizes unranked; conceals 30,131; bolsters 59,091; 4 of 4 past 10,000, 4 past 20,000.

fixes: writer flag closed: the paper body names the Martu throughout (Martu hunters in the Little Sandy Desert, "Because Martu burn when they hunt small prey"); the abstract only says Aboriginal; source now points to the PMC full text, which states both

items.subtype: Most nearly mean: underlined phrase or phrase options
items.passage:
The following text is adapted from Anne Thackeray Ritchie’s 1873 novel Old Kensington. Frank Raban has been searching for George, the missing brother of Dolly Vanborough, and is now walking with Dolly’s mother.

All that long day [Frank] had followed up every trace, been everywhere, questioned every one, including Rhoda, without result. When Dolly came to meet them, he thought she looked anxious enough already, and he <u>made light of</u> his long efforts, and shrugged his shoulders.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the phrase “made light of” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: To make light of something is to treat it as unimportant. Frank has searched all day without success, but seeing that Dolly already looks anxious, he shrugs and minimizes how hard he has tried, so that she will not worry more. He plays down his efforts.

A.why_wrong: This reads light as illumination, as if Frank explained his efforts. Instead he shrugs them off, which hides rather than explains how hard he has searched.

C.why_wrong: Taking pride in his efforts would draw attention to them, the opposite of shrugging them off to spare an already anxious Dolly.

D.why_wrong: Frank clearly remembers his long efforts; the text describes how he presents them to Dolly, not any confusion about them.

sources.what: Text of Old Kensington by Anne Thackeray Ritchie (1873), Project Gutenberg 36235; adapted by beginning at the second sentence of the paragraph, naming Frank in brackets, and omitting the sentence “He had come now in the faint hope of finding him at home after all.” between the two sentences shown

items.notes: Subject: literature. Key letter B. Phrasal target whose parts suggest other senses (light as brightness). Steps: 1 (anxious Dolly plus the shrug fix the sense). Excerpt copied exactly apart from the bracketed name. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): Shed light on 2,722; Played down 1,115; Took pride in 991; Lost track of 2,581; 0 of 4 past 10,000, 0 past 20,000.

fixes: source note completed: the excerpt also omits "He had come now in the faint hope of finding him at home after all." between its two sentences

items.passage: For more than a decade, photographer LaToya Ruby Frazier documented her grandmother, her mother, and herself in their hometown of Braddock, Pennsylvania, a former steelmaking community. The resulting photographs, published in The Notion of Family (2014), are deeply ______: many capture private moments in the everyday lives of the three women.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Personal means concerning one’s own private life. Frazier photographed her own grandmother, mother, and herself, and the text says the images capture private moments in their daily lives, so the photographs are deeply personal.

B.why_wrong: Commercial work is made to sell a product or service. These photographs show the private lives of Frazier’s own family, the opposite of advertising.

C.why_wrong: Nothing in the text says the photographs are funny.

D.why_wrong: Abstract images do not show recognizable people or things, but these photographs show Frazier’s family members.

sources.what: LaToya Ruby Frazier: photographs of her Grandma Ruby, her mother, and herself in Braddock, Pennsylvania; The Notion of Family (Aperture, 2014); images of personal spaces and intensely private moments

items.notes: Subject: humanities (photography). Key letter A. Restatement after the colon (private moments of her own family). Steps: 1. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): personal 1,149; commercial 4,708; humorous 5,911; abstract 9,239; 0 of 4 past 10,000, 0 past 20,000.

items.passage: Indian American composer Reena Esmail ______ two musical worlds. After studying Hindustani classical music in North India as a Fulbright scholar, she began composing works that bring together Indian and Western classical traditions, and she cofounded Shastra, an organization connecting Indian musical traditions with the West.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: To bridge two things is to connect them. The next sentence says Esmail writes works that bring together Indian and Western classical traditions and helped found an organization that connects Indian music with the West, so she links the two musical worlds.

A.why_wrong: Dividing the two worlds would mean keeping them apart, but Esmail’s works bring them together.

B.why_wrong: To predate is to come earlier in time. Both classical traditions are centuries older than Esmail, and the text is about how she joins them.

D.why_wrong: Nothing suggests that Esmail makes fun of either tradition; she studied one closely and writes music drawing on both.

sources.what: Reena Esmail: Indian-American composer who bridges Indian and Western classical music; Fulbright-Nehru scholarship to North India to study Hindustani music; cofounder of Shastra, which connects Indian musical tradition with the West

items.notes: Subject: humanities (music). Key letter C. Blank in the first sentence, restated in the next (bring together, connects). Steps: 1. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): divides 20,416; predates unranked; bridges 9,445; mocks 32,459; 3 of 4 past 10,000, 3 past 20,000.

items.passage: Each spring, bogong moths migrate hundreds of kilometers to cool caves and rock crevices in the Australian Alps. There they remain ______ throughout the summer: densely clustered on the cave walls, the moths stop feeding and stay inactive until autumn, when they return to their breeding grounds.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Dormant means inactive, as if asleep. After the colon, the text says the moths stop feeding and stay inactive until autumn, which describes a dormant state.

A.why_wrong: Restless creatures move about constantly, but these moths stay inactive all summer.

B.why_wrong: Nothing in the text describes the moths attacking anything; they simply rest on the cave walls.

C.why_wrong: Solitary means alone, but the moths are densely clustered together.

sources.what: Bogong moth: spring migration of up to about 965 km to the Australian Alps, aestivation (remaining dormant) over summer in cool caves and crevices without feeding, return to breeding grounds in autumn

items.notes: Subject: natural science (entomology). Key letter D. Restatement after the colon (stop feeding, stay inactive). Steps: 1. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): restless 2,476; aggressive 11,138; solitary 2,633; dormant 16,629; 2 of 4 past 10,000, 0 past 20,000.

items.passage: Both written and spoken language are ______ to the films of Ho-Chunk artist Sky Hopinka. His experimental work regularly incorporates English and chinuk wawa, an Indigenous language of the Pacific Northwest that Hopinka has also taught, into its subtitles, voice-overs, and poems.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?
items.explanation: Central means of the greatest importance. The second sentence says Hopinka’s films regularly use two languages in their subtitles, voice-overs, and poems, so language is at the heart of his work.

A.why_wrong: Incidental means minor or occurring only by chance. Language appears regularly and in many forms in Hopinka’s films, so it is not a minor element.

C.why_wrong: Nothing suggests that language damages Hopinka’s films; it is something he uses throughout them.

D.why_wrong: Hopinka has even taught chinuk wawa, and the text gives no sign that language is strange or new to his work.

sources.what: MacArthur Foundation, Sky Hopinka (2022 Fellow): both written and spoken language is integral to much of his film and video work; his films use English and chinuk wawa in subtitles, voice-overs, and poems

items.notes: Subject: humanities (film). Key letter B. Blank in the first sentence, restated by the next. Steps: 1. Raw ranks, tools/data/freq.txt (rarest content word, printed form): incidental 19,860; central 3,784; harmful 22,343; unfamiliar 8,144; 2 of 4 past 10,000, 1 past 20,000.

items.passage:
The following text is from E. W. Howe’s 1883 novel The Story of a Country Town. The narrator has just learned that Mateel, the former wife of his uncle Jo, is to marry another man.

The pity and friendliness I had formerly <u>entertained</u> for Mateel vanished with the messenger who brought me the letter announcing her contemplated marriage to Clinton Bragg, though my first feeling was of horror and indignation at a step which seemed so indelicate and cruel.
items.stem: As used in the text, what does the word “entertained” most nearly mean?
items.explanation: As used in the text, “entertained” means felt. The narrator says the pity and friendliness he once had toward Mateel disappeared when he heard of her marriage plans; entertained names those feelings he used to have.

A.why_wrong: To entertain can mean to amuse, but the narrator is not amusing pity and friendliness; he is describing feelings he once had.

B.why_wrong: To entertain can mean to host guests, but pity and friendliness are feelings, not visitors.
